correctness.rationale: For fixed n-vertex tree, Prüfer excess degree vector t_i>=0 sums n-2. For 0<q<1, strict convexity of log(1+q^d) and majorization make path unique minimum and star unique maximum. For physical q=-r in [-1/3,0), positive excess contributions h_r(k) lie between h_r(2) and h_r(1); inequality 2h_r(2)>h_r(1), equivalent to r(1+r)(1-r-r^3)>0, makes star unique minimum, path maximum. For subcubic trees degree count (k+2,n-2-2k,k) produces exact step factor 1+q(1-q)^2/(1+q²)^2. Independently enumerated all Prüfer words n=4,5,6 for q=+/-1/3, verified endpoints and subcubic ratios. Proof applies to all n>=4, actual physical depolarizing p up to 1.
